item.title: Texas House District 87 Caroline Fairly talks elections, legislative session
item.description: Texas House District 87 Representative Caroline Fairly sat down with KAMR Local 4 News reporter Princess Bryant to talk about the aftermath of the Texas primaries, the upcoming November election, the 90th Texas Legislative Session, and the Panhandle Leadership program.

item.title: Happy man indicted in Ellis County for 20 charges related to child sexual abuse
item.description: A Happy, Texas man has been indicted with 20 counts by an Ellis County Grand Jury last week.

item.title: 'Breezy' Fire in Carson County, 116 acres burned; 100% contained
item.description: The Texas A&M Forest Service reports that a fire is burning near Skellytown, and multiple crews are responding.

item.title: Panhandle boys basketball claims 1st State Title: PHS boys, girls crowned 2026 Champs
item.description: The Panhandle boys basketball team defeats San Augustine 61-58, to claim the program's first State Title in their first appearance.

item.title: Let's Talk About It: Clint Brakebill, award winning sports broadcaster
item.description: Award winning sports broadcaster, Clint Brakebill, is going out on top. After more than a decade of working as Sports Director at KAMR Local 4, Brakebill will be signing off this month and heading to Anna, Texas.

item.title: Amarillo College Board of Regents hosts special meeting Thursday on 'post-forensic audit actions'
item.description: The Amarillo College Board of Regents is set to host a special meeting on Thursday evening, which will include a review of the fiscal year 2024-2025 audit as well as discussions of possible actions in the wake of its recent independent forensic audit.

item.title: Jane Doe sues Amarillo Native and Author Amy Griffin, claiming her memoir 'The Tell' contains stolen stories
item.description: Amarillo native and author Amy Griffin is facing a lawsuit from an alleged former classmate who claims in a lawsuit filed earlier this month that the stories of sexual abuse detailed in Griffin's memoir "The Tell" are not Griffin's but rather her own.

item.title: 'Yellow' Fire in Moore, Hartley, Oldham counties still burning Wednesday; 14,374 acres, 90% contained
item.description: The Texas A&M Forest Service reported the Yellow Fire was estimated to have impacted 8,500 acres as of 9:25 a.m. on Wednesday, and was approximately 30% contained.
